title: EY is creating a 'value realization' office to make sure its AI spending pays off
excerpt: AI can't be managed by any existing department, so the Big Four firm EY is creating a new one. It's called the AI Value Realization Office.
content_html:
By Polly Thompson

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

AI can't be managed by any existing department, so EY is creating a new one.

The Big Four firm is setting up a new function called the "AI Value Realization Office" to centralize its AI spending and ensure the technology delivers measurable impact.

Dan Diasio, EY's global consulting AI leader, told Business Insider the firm expects the office to be fully operational within a couple of months.

Its job is to govern AI spending, drive returns, monitor usage, decide which AI initiatives to scale, and oversee how AI reshapes jobs.

Most companies allocate corporate budgets along departmental lines. However, AI spending and its potential payoff can cut across IT, finance, sales, HR, and operations, said Diasio.

"If you fund by department, you end up addressing a bunch of use cases inside of each of the functions. And what that often means is that you're leaving a lot of value on the table," he said.

EY-Parthenon research found that 75% of the potential enterprise value from AI comes from horizontal value streams — meaning across multiple functions — compared with 25% from projects contained within individual functions, Diasio said.

The AI office will govern the value strategy, looking not just at the dollar-for-dollar calculation but at a broader assessment of whether AI initiatives are changing business performance, Diasio said.

It "will help make sure that funding flows where the biggest opportunities are," he said.

Creating a corporate function to manage a growing cost or risk isn't a new idea. Modern-day HR departments emerged during the Great Depression as companies sought more systematic ways to hire and fire workers, while treasury teams took shape in the 1970s, when floating exchange rates made currency movements a bigger risk for multinational companies.

The AI value realization office is the modern-day equivalent, reallocating a set of responsibilities scattered across finance, technology, and other teams to a strategic function in its own right.

'Client zero'

The Big Four professional services pitch themselves as "client zero" for the AI future. By testing the technology on their own employees and operations, they can show clients what works — and sell them advice on doing the same.

The firms have also committed billions to the new technology. In 2023, EY said $1.4 billion went toward building the foundation for the EY.ai platform.

Like all businesses, AI providers' move to change pricing models has put pressure on professional services firms to use the technology effectively and limit costs.

EY has implemented an "invisible" AI router behind some of its specialized AI tools. The router directs employees to the best model for the task at hand, and has helped reduce token consumption by 60% since its implementation in April, alongside other governance strategies.

Saving measures are also becoming more important to clients as they get a clearer idea of what AI actually costs, said Diasio. Many started by experimenting while AI providers subsidized some of the expenses. Now they are confronting the real price tag and asking EY how to organize themselves as they scale AI.

In an EY US AI Pulse survey released in July, 98% of 534 senior decision-makers said token spending had made them reconsider their approach. The survey was conducted between April and May.

So far, companies have generally paid for AI by tightening budgets across the board and reallocating money, said Diasio. Giving AI governance more clout — through a function like the AI value realization office — will be a "critical part" of how EY's clients move forward, said Diasio.

Most clients aren't setting up dedicated AI offices yet, Diasio added.

"It's something that I imagine over time will become a function," he said. "The focus is beginning to shift more toward what the organization looks like on the other side of this."

content_html_zh:
作者：Polly Thompson 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

任何现有部门都无法管理人工智能，因此安永正在创建一个新部门。

这家四大公司正在设立一个名为“人工智能价值实现办公室”的新职能，以集中其人工智能支出并确保该技术产生可衡量的影响。

安永全球咨询人工智能负责人 Dan Diasio 告诉《商业内幕》，该公司预计该办公室将在几个月内全面投入运营。

它的职责是管理人工智能支出、推动回报、监控使用情况、决定扩展哪些人工智能计划，以及监督人工智能如何重塑就业。

大多数公司按照部门分配公司预算。 然而，迪亚西奥表示，人工智能支出及其潜在回报可以跨越 IT、财务、销售、人力资源和运营领域。

“如果你按部门提供资金，你最终会解决每个职能内部的一堆用例。 这通常意味着你留下了很多价值，”他说。

Diasio 表示，EY-Parthenon 研究发现，人工智能带来的 75% 的潜在企业价值来自横向价值流（即跨多个职能部门），而 25% 来自单个职能部门内的项目。

迪亚西奥表示，人工智能办公室将管理价值战略，不仅关注美元对美元的计算，还会更广泛地评估人工智能计划是否正在改变业务绩效。

他说，这“将有助于确保资金流向最有机会的地方”。

创建一个公司职能来管理不断增长的成本或风险并不是一个新想法。 现代人力资源部门是在大萧条时期出现的，当时公司寻求更系统的方式来雇用和解雇员工，而财务团队则在 20 世纪 70 年代形成，当时浮动汇率使货币波动对跨国公司构成更大的风险。

人工智能价值实现办公室相当于现代的办公室，它将分散在财务、技术和其他团队中的一系列职责重新分配给自己的战略职能。

“零客户”

四大专业服务将自己定位为人工智能未来的“零客户”。 通过在自己的员工和运营中测试该技术，他们可以向客户展示什么是有效的，并向他们推销同样做法的建议。

这些公司还为新技术投入了数十亿美元。 安永表示，2023 年将投入 14 亿美元为 EY.ai 平台奠定基础。

与所有企业一样，人工智能提供商改变定价模式的举措给专业服务公司带来了有效使用该技术并限制成本的压力。

安永在其一些专门的人工智能工具背后实施了一个“隐形”人工智能路由器。 该路由器将员工引导至手头任务的最佳模型，自 4 月份实施以来，与其他治理策略一起，已帮助减少了 60% 的代币消耗。

迪亚西奥表示，随着客户更清楚地了解人工智能的实际成本，节省措施对客户来说也变得更加重要。 许多人都是从试验开始的，而人工智能提供商则补贴了部分费用。 现在，他们面临着真正的价格标签，并询问安永在扩展人工智能时如何组织自己。

在安永美国 7 月发布的 AI Pulse 调查中，534 名高级决策者中的 98% 表示，代币支出让他们重新考虑了自己的做法。 该调查是在四月至五月期间进行的。

迪亚西奥表示，到目前为止，企业普遍通过全面收紧预算和重新分配资金来支付人工智能费用。 迪亚西奥表示，通过人工智能价值实现办公室等职能赋予人工智能治理更大的影响力，将成为安永客户前进的“关键部分”。

迪亚西奥补充说，大多数客户尚未设立专门的人工智能办公室。

“我想随着时间的推移，这将成为一种功能，”他说。 “焦点开始更多地转向组织的另一面。”
